Orbit and atmosphere held broadly comparable; qualitative speculation only

scenes.label: SLOW THE SPIN
scenes.text: What if a day lasted forty eight hours? Imagine Earth gradually spinning more slowly, not stopping suddenly.

scenes.label: SAME YEAR, LONGER DAY
scenes.text: Our trip around the Sun stays the same. The change in this thought experiment is the daily rotation.

scenes.label: MORE TIME IN SUNLIGHT
scenes.text: A place could spend longer under sunlight, then longer in darkness, reshaping daily heating and cooling.

scenes.label: WEATHER GETS COMPLICATED
scenes.text: Rotation also matters for weather. Predicting the new winds would require a model, not just a guess.

scenes.label: BIOLOGY HAS A CLOCK
scenes.text: Living things follow biological rhythms. A longer light and dark cycle would challenge those familiar schedules.

scenes.label: DO NOT DOUBLE EVERYTHING
scenes.text: A longer day would not simply double everything. The interesting question is how the whole system adapts.
